title: Henry of Navarre to Ségur, BnF 500 de Colbert 401 ff. 233, 239, 288v (1585-86), Navarre key A

steps.what: Gallica IIIF fetched with a browser User-Agent.
ff. 233, 239, 288v transcribed from full-resolution images (and f. 143, now segur1583).
Frequencies of the upper figures mod 5 show blocks of five: an alphabetical syllabary.
Catherine de Médicis letters under random keys of the same shape; 64-start model 47-90 %, corrected 54-start model 96.6 %.
Structured annealer with the clear French as context recovers the key; syllabary start corrected from 64 to 54 by the reading.
Three letters read in substance; word-signs partly glossed.
Whole volume swept for further letters in this key: none; f. 366 found (probably this key). (The f. 333 reading with Tomokiyo's f. 321 key in the same session is now navarre1586.)
f. 366 (24 tokens) tried with both keys; two of three lines do not read.
Design-constrained annealer (alphabetical homophone counts) on the ff. 233 set: whole letter key from seed 0, 287 of 290 letter tokens (99.0 %) against key_v4.json.

Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): he wrote that he had independently solved it in 2024 but never published it; kept in the ciphertext-only list with that note. In Oct 2026 he specified that his saved decryptions (15 Oct 2024) cover ff. 143, 233, 239 and 288v.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 470 tokens, 103 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.066 per letter; random keys -4.259 (z 15.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.698 (mean -2.734, z 17.4); annealer on the real text -2.564. Verdict: pass.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): segur keeps key A (ff. 233, 239, 288v; f. 366 noted as 'probably this key', open, and kept out of documents[] because its key is not shown); f. 333 with Tomokiyo's f. 321 key moved to navarre1586; f. 143 (1583, another key) moved to segur1583.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the three transcriptions, the edited reading reading.md and the decoder output decode_v4.txt, key key_v4.json. Lasry's own 2024 decryptions are private and not in the repository.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): f. 288v re-read with the word-sign values given in reading.md's notes: the slip builds French sentences with scattered open name and date signs. Per-document C overturned to B. Claim unchanged.

Key replay (docs/_replay.py): key_v4.json applied to ct_233/239/288.txt and compared with the bold passages of reading.md: 126 of 146 words exact (86.3%), 14 differing with no letter-level mark. The reading now brackets each letter the key does not give; no letter changed. After: 129 of 147 words exact (87.8%), 16 emended and marked, 2 unread, 0 unmarked, 20 open word-signs.

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026), each letter separately from the bold runs of its own section of reading.md (clear French, the English translation and f. 366 left out). Holes: unidentified word-signs in braces, words marked [?], letters supplied in [ ], and the unread stretches marked with an ellipsis inside a cipher run. f. 233 68 words 9 unread; f. 239 24 words 7 unread (pieces, with its slipped 66, among them: the one-digit-slip rule needs the surviving period key); f. 288v 74 words 17 unread. The recorded 0.984 for each letter was one whole-file figure. Result: read share 0.984 -> f233 0.868, f239 0.708, f288v 0.770 (133/166 over the three); all three letters and the target move from read to read in part; fraction_read by tokens (466/482, glossed word-signs counted) unchanged.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.066; polyphony 0.0; 16 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.564

outcome.method_basis: A syllabary residue test and a structured annealer with the letters' clear French as language-model context rebuilt the ff. 233/239/288v key, confirmed on matched controls; Tomokiyo's sibling f. 321 key (on cryptiana before the attempt) has different offsets and was not used for these letters.
outcome.notes: ff. 233, 239, 288v deciphered with key A, recovered ciphertext-only; read in part by the read bar over cipher words (16 Nov 2026): f. 233 59/68 (86.8%), f. 239 17/24 (70.8%), f. 288v 57/74 (77.0%), 133/166 in all. Open: the word-signs and numbers 180, 215?, 900, and words resting on doubtful or slipped figures. f. 366 (probably this key) left open and outside the documents; f. 333 (Tomokiyo's f. 321 key) is navarre1586; f. 143 (1583, another key) is segur1583.

credits.note: saved decryptions of ff. 233, 239, 288v dated 15 Oct 2024 (with f. 143, another key; see segur1583), unpublished

outcome.fraction_read_source: validation.tsv (mk_validation.py, ff. 233/239/288v with key_v4.json): 482 non-null tokens, 466 with a value, 16 unread word-signs and numbers (X, gla, gna, pe, pu, e, H, L, Ne, qua, 180, 215?, 900); glossed word-signs counted with their gloss.

gaps.detail: line 3 reads escri; lines 1-2 decode to non-French, probably names in the king's spelling

gaps.item: words resting on doubtful or slipped figures: avec, contracte, Eglises, the year 1579 and the pair 87 52 in f. 233; pieces and vou[s] in f. 239; peine, escrire, son[t] and the closing name or place (Valen[ce?]) in f. 288v
gaps.detail: the digits were re-read at 2x and 3x on the Gallica images and stand; whether 20 (avec, contracte, Valen-h) and the adjacent-value figures (pieces in f. 239 among them) are the encipherer's slips or values of the key can only be settled by the key sheet, which is not in the volume; vou[s] and son[t] lack a letter in the cipher itself. Counted as holes in the cipher-word read share (16 Nov 2026)

texts.label: f. 233, Henry of Navarre to Ségur, October 1585
texts.summary: Navarre, a month after the bull of excommunication, tells Ségur in Germany to conclude promptly, if possible with Duke [John] Casimir or with his consent, to raise the largest levy he can and march it at once; Clervant is to raise the two thousand reiters he is bound to furnish under the contract with the Churches.
texts.note: Read share over cipher words only (16 Nov 2026): the bold runs of reading.md's f. 233 section, 68 cipher words, 9 unread ({X}, {gla}, {180}, the unread pair before et, and the doubtful avec[?], contracte[?], Eglises[?], et[?], 1579[?]): 59/68. The earlier 0.984 was one figure for the whole file (translation and f. 366 included) copied to all three letters.

texts.label: f. 239, Henry of Navarre to Ségur, Montauban, February 1586
texts.summary: From Montauban: spare no means, succour us in all diligence, set every piece in motion. The postscript in another hand adds Drake's 'very great prize' (the sack of Santo Domingo, January 1586).
texts.note: Read share over cipher words only (16 Nov 2026): the bold runs of reading.md's f. 239 section (postscript included), 24 cipher words, 7 unread ({900}, {gne}, {gna}, pieces (pi-e-bi-es, 66 for 60/61: a one-figure slip in a key recovered here, so the slip rule does not apply), {e}, vou[s], {na}): 17/24; 18/24 with the context gloss {na} = nouvelles counted. The earlier 0.984 was the whole-file figure copied to all three letters.

texts.label: f. 288v (slip), Henry of Navarre to Ségur, 1 April 1586
texts.summary: Navarre is in extreme anxiety at having no news and asks Ségur to make, if he can, the greatest levy ever made; the two thousand reiters Clervant is bound to furnish are very necessary. The levy marched in 1587 to the disaster of Auneau.

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. reading.md's notes resolve most word signs from context ({gne} = Je, {na} = nouvelles/affaires, {Ra} = faictes, {qu} = vous), and with them the slip reads: "Je suis en extreme peine de n'avoir eu de vos nouvelles ...; je ne sçay [par où vous] escrire, ne à qui, ne en quel estat sont nos affaires ... faictes s'il vous est possible la plus grande levée qui ayt esté faite". Open: the date sign {e}, the name signs {H} {L}, {pe} {pu} and {qua}.

texts.note: Read share over cipher words only (16 Nov 2026): the bold runs of reading.md's f. 288v section, 74 cipher words, 17 unread (word-signs {gne}, {na} x2, {e}, {pe}, {pu}, {Ra}, {qu}, {H}, {L}, {qua}, {Ne}; peine[?], e[s]crire, son[t]; the unread stretch and Valen[ce?] at the end): 57/74; 62/74 (0.838) with the context glosses of the 22 Oct reading audit ({gne} = Je, {na}, {Ra} = faictes, {qu} = vous) counted. The earlier 0.984 was the whole-file figure.

prior.where: No plaintext of ff. 233, 239, 288v found in print or online. George Lasry's saved decryptions of 15 Oct 2024 cover ff. 143, 233, 239 and 288v (his note to the project, Oct 2026); unpublished; earlier reported 25 Sept 2026 as an independent 2024 solution. Tomokiyo's f. 321 key (a sibling, different values) was on cryptiana.
